items.evidence: Line 3 opens '## The bottom line', followed in order by '**1. What FRUS answers directly.**' (line 5), '**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.**' (line 7) and '**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.**' (line 9). The first finding ('### 1. In China, corruption became Washington's stated reason for reluctance on aid (1944–1948)') comes at line 24, after Scope and Decisions; nothing precedes the three parts but the title.

No percent sign appears, and every figure names its set and base: 'about one document in a hundred across the 553 volumes of the series'; 'about 311,000 documents, of which 3,036 use the words (3,020 once sixteen documents printed twice are counted once)'; 'none in the thirteen 1981–88 volumes indexed'; '27 documents in 21 volumes join bribery to consuls and fees'; 'only eleven of the nearly seven hundred series they describe start before 1940'; 'found in 550 of 551 volumes'; 'All forty contained a form of the words, and 37 used them for official or financial wrongdoing'; 'The 1947 China volume holds more documents using the words (71) than any other volume in the series'; the decade rates ('about three in every thousand documents in the 1930s and about twenty in the 1960s and 1970s') are given 'against the number of dated documents in that decade'. The least-anchored figure, 'The Church subcommittee is named in 42 documents, but only three join it to bribery or payments', still names its set, with the universe fixed by the Scope paragraph.

All 19 cited documents carry the printed-edition form with a link, e.g. 'Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969–1976, Volume E–9, Part 2, Documents on the Middle East Region, 1973–1976, Document 161 (https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1969-76ve09p2/d161)' and 'Foreign Relations of the United States, 1955–1957, Near East: Jordan-Yemen, Volume XIII, Document 16 (https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1955-57v13/d16)'. The four short forms ('same volume, Document 135 (https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1958-60v01/d135)', 'same volume, Document 204 (…/frus1961-63v22/d204)', 'Also Document 152 (…/frus1969-76ve09p2/d152)', 'same volume, Document 248 (…/frus1977-80v03/d248)') each follow the full citation of that volume in the same or the preceding bullet and each carries its link. No bare id pair and no title-only citation appears; the unfollowed threads in Read next (Somoza, Mobutu, Vesco, Zahedi, the 1953 Philippine election) cite no document.

Part 3 states its gaps as searches: '(a) After 1980. A search for the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act by name found four documents, all from 1977–80, and none in the thirteen 1981–88 volumes indexed. Relaxing it to "corrupt practices" found one document in those volumes, and the general corruption words fifty-nine.' and closes with the controls: 'Each search ran with a positive check (the phrase "Department of State", found in 550 of 551 volumes) and an impossible-word check (found nowhere) in the same pass.' (b) and (d) give their searches' counts ('The Church subcommittee is named in 42 documents, but only three join it to bribery or payments'; '27 documents in 21 volumes join bribery to consuls and fees'; 'only eleven of the nearly seven hundred series they describe start before 1940'). (c) is a reading observation rather than a search (in the Lockheed telegrams the names are 'still withheld as not declassified'; Lot 79 F 80 'could not resolve it to a series'), grounded in the documents and the finding aids rather than asserted.

No SQL keyword, table or column name, or file path appears anywhere in the overview. The only 'frus…/d…' strings sit inside the history.state.gov URLs that J3 requires (e.g. 'https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1947v07/d908'); never a bare pair. The working record is referred to as '(see the memo)' and 'the app's bundled finding aids', with no path. Strings such as 'Lot 54 D 270', 'entry A1 3051B', 'creator identifier 10481258' and 'Job 79-T00472A' are NARA and CIA archival identifiers, not index ids.

judge:s2.rankingReason: s2 first: six findings on 19 read documents follow the question's decisions themselves (aid withheld or conditioned in China, Vietnam and Korea; Lockheed's fallout managed with Riyadh, Bonn and Tokyo; the UN agreement and the 1977 law), every gap is a search with its terms, its volumes and a positive and an impossible-word control in the same pass, the archival pointers resolve Lot 54 D 270 to its ten NARA series and keep the two channels apart, and the collection gives each of the 19 a note and a verified excerpt with the unfollowed threads named. s7 second: a tighter, well-written five-case overview on 11 documents, with the 1875 Venezuela claims case and a sharp Vietnam 'limits of leverage' finding, but a thinner base, one figure with an unnamed set ('about two in five of the documents'), 'roughly one document in 115' with its denominator left to the Scope line, a 'kleptocracy' gap that measures a word no contemporary used, and lots 54D270 and 59D95 left unresolved that s2 resolved.

refute:s2.fabricationDetails: None. overview.md holds 30 double-quoted strings (refuter/quotes_check.out). Twenty are document quotations: the 18 bullet quotations under Findings 1-6, 'even if untrue' in the Finding 2 preamble, and the Chinese information chief's 'play up the cases ...' in Finding 1; the other ten are search terms or titles ('corrupt practices', 'Department of State', 'corruption' twice, 'corrupt', 'corrupted', 'Questionable payments', 'questionable', 'question', and the collection's name) with no document attached.
